title: EU AI Act Article 55 GPAI Transparency Obligations — What General-Purpose AI Providers Must Disclose
context: 2026-08-26 — Article 55 in force since 2 August 2026; GPAI providers must now publish detailed training data summaries and technical documentation
body: Article 55 of the EU AI Act creates a binding transparency obligation for all providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models. Unlike the watermarking requirements of Article 50 or the literacy obligations of Article 4, Article 55 requires providers to publish a detailed summary of the content used to train their model. This summary must be sufficiently detailed that downstream deployers — and the AI Office — can verify that the training data complies with EU copyright law (Articles 53(1)(c) and 53(1)(d)). The deadline is now: Article 55 entered into force on 2 August 2026. Providers who fail to publish their training data summary face enforcement action from the AI Office under Article 89. The Council of AI's verified measurement credential maps to this obligation: a signed benchmark run that includes a training-data provenance axis provides machine-readable evidence that a model's data disclosure is complete and honest. Three practical steps: (1) assemble a training-data summary in the AI Office's designated template by 30 September 2026 at the latest; (2) publish the summary to a persistent, versioned URL; (3) obtain a verified measurement credential that attests to the summary's completeness — this converts a self-declaration into an independently verifiable attestation.
